before: A match guard adds if condition after a pattern. Some(n) if n > 0 handles only present positive values; the following Some(_) still handles other present values. _ ignores a matched value.

Match selects the first matching arm whose guard succeeds. A guard is not a replacement for covering remaining cases. This classification keeps None distinct from a present zero. The returned string literals have type &'static str: their text is available for the entire program, not allocated inside the function.
Expected output or behavior: positive. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare None with Some(-1) and explain why absence is not the same as a nonpositive value. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
